title: Unified client SDK: cursored paging, durable retries, and buffered streaming contract
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Multiple teams have implemented client behavior independently and we are seeing divergent runtime semantics around paging cursors, retry/backoff behavior, and streaming delivery. This ticket defines a single cross-language contract that client libraries (Python, TypeScript, Go) must implement so application developers get predictable behavior across deployments (hosted, dedicated, private).

Goals:
- Define canonical cursor-based pagination semantics (cursor format, determinism, resumption).
- Specify idempotency and retry behavior for both unary and streaming endpoints (including exponential backoff, jitter, and which errors are retriable).
- Establish a buffered streaming API surface that supports both server-push partials (token/fragment streaming) and client-controlled flow (backpressure, max buffer).
- Define compatibility and deprecation policy to avoid breaking changes across minor releases.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Backwards compatibility required for existing major version (v2.x). Minor releases may add non-breaking features.
- Network environments include high-latency on-prem and low-latency cloud; streaming must degrade gracefully.
- SDKs must be idiomatic per language but provide consistent end-user observable behavior (same error classes, same retry semantics, same pagination guarantees).
scope:
In scope:
- Detailed API contract for cursored pagination for list endpoints (cursor encoding, page_size semantics, empty pages).
- Retry policy document covering transient errors, 5xxs, network failures, and client-side timeouts; explicit idempotency guidance for create/update calls.
- Streaming API abstraction: buffered reader/iterator for TS/Python, channel-based for Go; documented buffer limits and backpressure hooks.
- Language-specific examples (Python async iterator, TS async generator, Go channel + context cancellation).
- Interop test suite definitions (integration tests against staging runtime) and CI gating.
- Deprecation policy text and compatibility matrix.

Deliverables:
- PRD + acceptance criteria (this ticket).
- Confluence design doc with wireframes and code samples.
- SDK reference impls in each language and interop tests.
- Release notes template and migration guide.
out_of_scope:
Out of scope:
- Implementing language SDKs (handled in separate ENG tickets once this spec is approved).
- Runtime/server-side changes beyond small compatibility toggles (those will be tracked in infra tickets).
- Long-term protocol redesign (e.g., switching from HTTP/2 to gRPC for streaming).
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs (Python, TS, Go) have language-idiomatic API signatures documented in the PRD and sample snippets for: listResources(cursor,page_size), streamGeneration(params) and sendWithIdempotency(token).

Cursor semantics: a cursor string is opaque to the client, stable across minor server changes, and encodes (server_version, offset). Clients must treat cursors as opaque and must resume list iteration deterministically when a cursor is supplied.

Pagination behavior: requesting page_size N returns at most N items and a next_cursor when more items exist; requesting with an out-of-range cursor yields a 410 with migration guidance (non-retriable).

Retry policy: default client policy implements exponential backoff with full jitter starting at 100ms, max backoff 10s, with a configurable max_attempts default 5; only errors in the spec (e.g., network ECONNRESET, 502, 503, 504) are retriable.
Clients must expose a hook to override retry policy per call.

Idempotency: SDKs must supply helper for idempotency tokens; server must accept idempotency keys for write operations. Spec defines which endpoints are idempotent by default and which require token to be safe to retry.

Streaming: SDKs expose an async/iterator (Python/TS) or channel (Go) that yields partial payloads as they arrive. The SDK must provide a configurable per-call buffer limit (default 16MB) and a backpressure callback that the application may use to pause/resume consuming. If the buffer overflows, the SDK must surface a clear BufferOverflow error and close the stream.

Compatibility: minor releases must not remove or rename public parameters; any behavioral changes must be behind feature flags for 2 minor release cycles. The SDK compatibility matrix document is published and linked in the PRD.
Interop tests: There is a CI job (sdk-interop) that runs the interop test suite for all three SDKs against staging; PRs touching SDK contracts fail CI if any interop tests regress.
Documentation: Confluence PRD, per-language quickstart, and migration guide are published and linked in the release notes.
decisions: Use opaque base64 URL-safe cursor string that contains server_version and index metadata instead of integer offsets to allow server-side reordering in the future.
Adopt exponential backoff with full jitter (100ms base, 2x multiplier, max 10s) as default to reduce thundering herd on retries.
Streaming API will be push-first with client-side buffering and backpressure hooks rather than pull-based demand model to keep cross-language surface consistent and simpler for users.
Expose retry/backoff configuration via a single RetryPolicy object across languages to make overriding consistent in SDKs.
Deprecation windows: announce deprecations in minor release N, remove after minor release N+2 (approx 6 months).
open_questions: Should the SDK expose a human-readable cursor decode helper for debugging? (Pros: debuggability; Cons: encourages reliance on cursor internals.)
What is the canonical error class mapping from HTTP status codes to language-specific exceptions (e.g., ResourceNotFound vs NotFoundError)? Need final mapping agreed with language leads.
Do we allow per-endpoint default buffer limits on streaming in server config that SDKs can read from discovery, or should SDK defaults be hardcoded in the client?

Edge-case: how should clients handle partial delivery plus a retriable transient error during streaming? (Current proposal: stream yields partials, attempt transparent retry only if the server can resume; otherwise surface a StreamIncomplete error with resume cursor if available.)

2026-02-12: Draft PRD created and shared with SDK and runtime leads (pinged @eng-sdk).
2026-02-15: Design review: agreed on opaque cursor and retry defaults; language leads requested explicit error mapping table (action: ENG-23459).
2026-02-18: Product review: prioritized idempotency helper and migration guide to reduce customer upgrade friction.
2026-02-20: Set up initial interop CI job (github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-interop/actions) and added placeholder tests for pagination and streaming.
2026-02-22: Received feedback from security: no KMS changes required for tokens but request to verify token storage patterns; security review set as follow-up.
Next steps: finalize error mapping, add code samples for each language, open ENG tickets for implementation and CI flakiness remediation.
